tasks.prompt: A system has technical write access to a repository, but the human only asked it to inspect a failing build. Decide what actions are permitted, what are prohibited, and what evidence is needed before any mutation. Keep capability and authority separate.
A product has a database, a knowledge base, source control, and a control-plane UI. Assign authoritative source ownership by fact class and identify where duplicated projections can become dangerous.

A CI pipeline is green, but a provider-backed feature has never been exercised against the real provider. Determine which claims are justified and design the minimum evidence needed to raise confidence.
A dashboard last refreshed 18 hours ago. The source API is currently unavailable. Design the correct user-visible state and explain what must not be shown as current fact.
Two independent reviewers disagree: one says a release is ready, the other found an unresolved authority leak. Produce a decision process that preserves the disagreement and avoids false consensus.
Design a minimal read adapter for an external provider that returns source identity, revision/ref, observation time, freshness, provenance, and semantic reliability without allowing writes.

A technically functional mobile dashboard feels generic and heavy on a low-end Android device. Propose the smallest redesign that improves perceived product quality without increasing runtime cost substantially.

An architecture has named roles, memory stores, governance documents, and many internal abstractions. Define a falsification test for whether a normal tab with a profile and persistent context would achieve the same operational value.
A new clean session must recover enough institutional state to continue a project without relying on conversation history. Specify the minimal cold-start evidence and failure conditions.
A system records lessons after each task. Define a test that distinguishes simple storage from operational learning that actually changes future behavior and is later validated.

Four specialist agents independently analyze the same problem, but none sees another agent's work until a final aggregator. Determine what can legitimately be called multi-agent and what cannot be called a mesh.
Define the minimum runtime evidence required to claim a cognitive mesh rather than several unrelated calls. Include topology, information flow, identity, and falsification criteria.
Define the minimum runtime evidence required to claim a dynamic agent population. Distinguish predeclared fixed roles from agents created and selected according to task demand.

A four-agent system appears better than one agent. Design an ablation study that can determine whether the improvement comes from a specific specialist, extra tokens, extra sampling, or actual interaction structure.
A mesh improves answer quality by 4 percent but uses 7 times more tokens and 5 times more latency than a single agent. Decide when it is justified and what additional evidence is required.

An agent proposes a change, another executes it, and the same second agent labels the result approved. Identify the governance defect and propose the minimum separation needed for trustworthy assurance.
A design document says a system has an internal civilization of agents, but logs only show one model call. Classify the claim epistemically and specify what evidence would be needed to promote it.
One node in a multi-agent workflow returns malformed output. Design behavior that preserves partial evidence, avoids silent repair claims, and still allows safe continuation when possible.
Compare star, chain, and peer mesh coordination for a task requiring architecture, engineering, adversarial review, and synthesis. State what empirical measurements would decide between them.

Create a compact rule set for promoting cognitive architecture claims from proposal to materialized, observed, causal, replicated, and operationally validated states. Prevent terminology from outrunning evidence.
